transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you into the clinic to see me today?

Hi. Well, what made me come in is that, for the past year or so, I've been having this issue where the smallest thing just pulls me off what I’m doing before I can even stop it. 

It could be a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office, or even just a random thought about my in-laws popping into my head. I just get completely derailed from my work, and I need to figure out how to get a handle on it.
Did you experience similar problems with attention and distractibility while growing up as a child, or did this begin solely in adulthood?

Looking back, yeah, it was definitely around when I was a kid, too. I remember teachers were always having to move my seat because I talked too much, or I'd just get up without asking. I also had a habit of blurting things out before they even finished asking the question. So, it definitely didn't just start in adulthood.
Do you still find yourself feeling restless, fidgety, or constantly on the go as an adult?

Yeah, I definitely do. Like, when I'm in meetings, I'm usually bouncing my knee, or I'll be clicking a pen, or just shifting around in my chair a lot. People have actually started giving me these looks... like they think I'm trying to rush them along, even when I'm really just trying to sit there and listen.
